extracted.intended_audience: applicants and representatives entering the European phase before the EPO (Euro‑PCT) — patent applicants, patent attorneys and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for completing and filing EPO Form 1200 to enter the European phase of a PCT application (Euro‑PCT), including procedural, documentary, fee, translation and representation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form 1200 / typewritten requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Form 1200 is recommended. The form should be typewritten or printed (Rule 50(2) EPC) to ensure that it is machine-readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is not enough space for required information, file an additional sheet indicating the number and heading of each continued section (e.g. "2 - Additional representative(s)"). Applicants should indicate their internal reference in the box above section 1 and in the corresponding box at the bottom of each page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels and copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 1200 and attachments must be filed direct with the EPO. They may be filed online, by fax, by post or in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online filing (EPO Online Filing, CMS/new online filing, Online Filing 2.0, Web‑Form Filing) is available and the online filing fee is less than filing in person, by post or by fax. Fax filing may require a paper confirmation only if the EPO specifically requests it. Form 1200 need only be filed in one copy. Special rules apply to sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts required on entry and time limit (Rule 159 and 162)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 159(1) EPC, on entry into the European phase applicants must perform the acts specified in Rules 159(1)(a) to (h) and 162(1) EPC within 31 months of the filing date or, if priority claimed, the (earliest) priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Euro‑PCT Guide Chapter 5 for details of the acts. Failure to perform required acts within the time limit can affect entitlement to proceed in the European phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated prosecution (PACE) and relation to early processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO PACE programme offers options to shorten processing time for search or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PACE requests filed before the end of the international phase will not be effective unless accompanied by an express request for early processing under Article 23(2) or 40(2) PCT. For other acceleration routes see the EPO notices (e.g. OJ EPO 2015, A94) and point 12 of the Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early processing request under Article 23(2)/40(2) PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Early processing of the application pursuant to Article 23(2)/40(2) PCT may be requested ("early entry into the European phase").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please note the requirements for an effective request and its legal consequences; see the 'Notes on EPO Form 1200' and the referenced guidance in point 12.1 of the Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of applicant information
rubrics_metrics.description: If on entry into the European phase the address, nationality, or country of residence or of place of business is missing for any applicant (as may occur under Rule 26.2bis(b) PCT), this information must be filed on a separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full applicant information to avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address for correspondence eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An address for correspondence may be given only by applicants who are not obliged to appoint a professional representative and have not appointed one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The address must be the applicant's own address and must be in an EPC contracting state. Addresses accepted for proceedings in the international phase but not fulfilling these conditions will not be accepted in proceedings before the EPO in the European phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirement (Articles 133 and 134 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants not having their residence or principal place of business in an EPC contracting state must be represented by a professional representative and act through him in all proceedings established by the EPC (Article 133(2) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2 of Form 1200 must always be completed if a professional representative or a legal practitioner entitled to act is appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorisation to act (Rule 152 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 152 certain professional representatives who identify themselves are required to file a signed authorisation only in particular circumstances; a legal practitioner entitled under Article 134(8) EPC or an employee acting under Article 133(3) EPC who is not a professional representative must file a signed authorisation unless an express prior authorisation is already on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an association registered with the EPO is appointed as representative (Rule 152(11) EPC), indicate the association's registered name and registration number. Use Form 1003 for individual authorisations and Form 1004 for general authorisations when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination — filing and payment condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for examination is not deemed to be filed until the examination fee has been paid (Article 94(1) and Rule 70(1) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be filed either up to six months from the date on which the international search report (or declaration under Article 17(2)(a) PCT) was published or within 31 months from the filing date or, where applicable, the earliest priority date, whichever period ends later. In practice this means submission within the 31‑month period, unless the ISR was published late.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination language and fee reduction conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons having their residence or principal place of business in an EPC contracting state with an official language other than English, French or German, and nationals of that state who are resident abroad, may file the request for examination in an admissible non‑EPO language (Article 14(4) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request for examination is filed in an admissible non‑EPO language in addition to the (pre‑crossed) request in the language of the proceedings, the examination fee is reduced by 30% provided the applicant is an SME, natural person, non‑profit organisation, university or public research organisation (Rule 6(4) EPC, Article 14(1) RFees). To benefit, the applicant must declare entitlement at the latest by payment of the fee (by crossing the box on the form or separately). If multiple applicants exist, for the reduction to apply each must qualify, but it is sufficient that only one of the multiple applicants is entitled to file documents in an admissible non‑EPO language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional copies of documents cited in supplementary European search report
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more additional sets of copies of the documents cited in the supplementary European search report can be ordered against payment of the flat‑rate fee(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 65 EPC and the fees schedule for ordering and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of documents forming basis for European proceedings (Section 6 / Rule 159(1)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application enters the European phase applicants must specify the application documents, as originally filed or as amended, on which the European grant procedure is to be based (Rule 159(1)(b) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6 allows applicants to indicate whether they wish to proceed with (a) the published documents (where amended claims under Article 19 PCT replace the originally filed claims) — in proceedings before the EPO as designated Office without PCT Chapter II (section 6.1), or (b) the documents on which the international preliminary examination report is based — in proceedings before the EPO as elected Office under PCT Chapter II (section 6.2). Sections 6.1 and 6.2 also provide the possibility to indicate that amended documents filed on entry into the European phase are to form the basis for the grant procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond to negative WO‑ISA/IPER/SISR and time limit (Rule 161)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the EPO has acted as ISA and, if applicable, IPEA or SISA, the applicant will be required to respond to any negative written opinion (WO‑ISA), to the negative international preliminary examination report (IPER) or to objections raised in the SISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time limit for response is six months from the invitation under Rule 161(1) EPC. Failure to respond in due time will lead to the application being deemed to be withdrawn (Rule 161(1) EPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments/comments filed on entry may constitute a response
rubrics_metrics.description: New amendments (Articles 28 and 41 PCT) and/or comments filed on entry into the regional phase before the EPO will be considered to constitute a response to the WO‑ISA, IPER or SISR if the applicant indicates on Form 1200 that such amendments/comments are to form the basis for further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, amendments under Article 19 and/or 34 PCT filed in the international phase and maintained on entry into the European phase by appropriate entries on Form 1200 may constitute a response, subject to certain requirements (see Guidelines for Examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of documents for additional‑fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must specify in the table on page 8 of Form 1200 the documents which are to be used for the European phase and therefore form the basis for calculation of any additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any exceptional circumstances needing further explanation must be clarified on an additional sheet. Only pages to be taken into account for calculation of the additional fee (Art. 2(1), item 1a RFees) should be indicated; pages replaced under Art. 19/34 that are to be substituted must not be indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during six‑month Rule 161 period — fee treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant can amend the application at any time within a non‑extendable period of six months from the communication under Rule 161(1) and (2) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages of amendments filed during the six‑month period under Rule 161 EPC are not taken into account in the calculation of the additional fee as part of the filing fee. Consequently, if amendments filed at this stage reduce the number of pages already paid for, no refund of the additional fee will be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten amendments — remedial invitation and refusal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: If application documents filed on entry into the European phase contain handwritten amendments, an invitation to remedy this deficiency will be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of non‑compliance the application will be refused. See the EPO notice concerning application of Rules 49 and 50 EPC to handwritten amendments (OJ EPO 2013, 603).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of amendments and indication of basis (Rule 137(4) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever amendments are filed, the applicant must identify them and indicate the basis for them in the application as filed (Rule 137(4) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to do so, the examining division may issue a communication under Rule 137(4) EPC requesting correction within a non‑extendable one‑month period. Failure to reply within that period will lead to the application being deemed to be withdrawn under Article 94(4) EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of test reports supplied in international proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has supplied test reports in proceedings before the EPO as International Preliminary Examining Authority, the EPO assumes that it may also use them in the European grant proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further action required unless otherwise indicated by the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of search results for priority applications (Rule 141(1) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each previous application whose priority is claimed, a copy of the search results produced by the authority with which the application was filed (Rule 141(1) EPC) has to be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation applies to European patent applications and international applications filed on or after 1 January 2011. The corresponding box on the form is to be crossed only if the copies are indeed supplied when filing the form. If a copy of the search results is included in the file by the EPO, no action by the applicant is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the international application (language and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was not published in an EPO official language, the applicant must furnish the EPO with a translation of that application in such a language within 31 months of the filing date or, where applicable, the (earliest) priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings in the European phase will be conducted in the language of the translation. The translation must include the description, the claims as originally filed, any text in the drawings, and the abstract. It must also include any indications under Rule 13bis.3 and 13bis.4 PCT for inventions relating to biological material and any published request for rectification (Rule 91.3(d) PCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the priority (previous) application (Rule 53(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 53(3) EPC, applicants may be invited by the EPO to file a translation of the previous (priority) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See OJ EPO 2013, 150 for further details on invitations to translate priority applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation‑fee selection and automatic debiting instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the automatic debiting procedure, validation fees will be debited only for states indicated on the form, unless the EPO receives a contrary instruction before the expiry of the payment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only tick the states for which you want validation fees debited automatically. Check national validation requirements (e.g. temporary exclusions) — the Notes include country‑specific information (example: Cambodia: pharmaceutical products excluded from patent protection until 2033; see OJ EPO 2018, A16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of communications under Rules 161/162 and Rule 70(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may waive his right to the communication under Rules 161(1) or (2) and 162 EPC. The applicant may also waive his right to be asked under Rule 70(2) EPC whether he wishes to proceed further with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form provides check boxes for these waivers; understand legal consequences before waiving (see 'Merkblatt zum Formblatt EPA 1200').

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature details and authorised signatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Under signature please print name and, in the case of legal persons, indicate the position within the company of the signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For employees (Art. 133(3) EPC) with general authorisation, include the general authorisation number where applicable. Use block letters for printed names as requested on the form.
